### Eastport

- **Type:** City
- **Recorded status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-08-12 (City Council unanimous vote)
- **Normalized date:** `2026-08-12` (exact)
- **Duration:** 180 days unless extended or terminated by the council, or until the two pending citizen-initiated data-center ordinances have been reviewed and decided, whichever occurs first
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `me-eastport-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Eastport City Council motion/ordinance (moved by Councilor Karen Raye), adopted 2026-08-12
- **What prompted it:** Specific proposed project: DeepGreen Holdings LLC's proposed underwater, tidal-powered AI data center in the Bay of Fundy/Western Passage (FERC preliminary-permit application filed February 2026), opposed by residents, the Eastport Coalition for Healthy Oceans (ECHO), and Passamaquoddy tribal officials; the moratorium gives the Council time to consult with the Planning Board on two citizen-initiated ordinances aimed at the project
- **Affected projects:** DeepGreen Holdings LLC's proposed underwater AI data center in the Western Passage/Bay of Fundy off Eastport (DeepGreen Western Passage SVP), a FERC preliminary-permit applicant scaled down from an original 400-acre/51-MW/170-turbine proposal to a 27.1-acre/15-MW/16-to-34-turbine proposal as of this pass; no preliminary permit had been granted.
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23. The City Council voted unanimously on 2026-08-12 to adopt a 180-day moratorium prohibiting any application, permit, license, or approval related to a commercial or industrial data center or AI computing facility, explicitly including land-based, underwater, and partially/fully submerged facilities, directly halting the DeepGreen underwater data center proposal. The Planning Board held a special public hearing on the related citizen-initiated ordinances on 2026-08-24; as of this pass, those ordinances (a permanent ban and a separate voter-approval requirement) remained under review, with the permanent-ban question expected before the Council at a special meeting. The August 24 Planning Board recommended adoption of a permanent ban with changes and dismissal of the separate voter-approval proposal; those recommendations are not council decisions. The disposition of both initiatives, any earlier end of the moratorium, and current legal force remain unverified. [VERIFY initiative decisions and current effect]
- **Outcome:** 180-day moratorium adopted specifically to halt the DeepGreen underwater data center proposal while the city reviews citizen-initiated ordinances that would permanently restrict or require voter approval for data center development.

- **What prompted it:** Preemptive; the town cited the absence of specific data center standards in its Land Use Ordinance/Comprehensive Plan, the experience of Wiscasset and Lewiston with inadequate regulatory frameworks, and a desire to protect the Georges River watershed and electrical infrastructure
- **Affected projects:** None identified; adopted preemptively.

No data center applications had been filed in Warren.
- **Outcome:** 180-day moratorium on data centers and accessory uses (including BESS, substations, cooling towers, and on-site generation accessory to a data center) adopted by town meeting vote to allow the town to develop permanent land use regulations.

## State-policy observations

These are raw observations with separate legal forms and review scopes. A bill, precursor memo, executive action and resolution are not interchangeable. Recorded enactment does not certify current legal force.

### LD 307 / HP 207, 132nd Legislature

- **Policy ID:** `me-ld-307-hp-207-132nd-legislature`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. Melanie Sachs; original bill page also identifies Rep. Drew Gattine on adopted amendment H-1051; Democratic
- **Recorded status:** Passed both chambers (House enactment vote 83-66, 2026-04-08); vetoed by Gov. Janet Mills 2026-04-24; House override attempt failed 72-65 (92 needed for 2/3) on 2026-04-29; Veto Sustained, 2026-04-29
- **Provisions:** Would have prohibited any municipality, state agency, or quasi-independent state entity from accepting applications or issuing permits, certificates, or approvals for development, construction, or operation of a data center with a load of 20 MW or more until 2027-11-01. Would have created the Maine Data Center Coordination Council to study ratepayer, grid reliability, environmental, host-community, data-sharing, impact fee, demand response, and community benefit agreement issues, with report due 2027-02-01.
- **Mechanism / scope:** statewide_moratorium; mixed
- **Legal effect:** failed
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** Proposed section 1 application and approval limitation would be repealed 2027-11-01; bill vetoed.
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://legislature.maine.gov/legis/bills/display_ps.asp?LD=307&snum=132>)

### LD 713 / HP 452, 132nd Legislature; Public Law 2025, c. 768

- **Policy ID:** `me-ld-713-hp-452-132nd-legislature-public-law-2026-c-768`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. Cloutier of Lewiston; Rep. Sayre of Kennebunk sponsored adopted House amendment H-1040; —
- **Recorded status:** Signed by Governor 2026-04-23; official chapter citation Public Law 2025, c. 768 (132nd Legislature, enacted in 2026). Effective 2026-07-29 under the official session-law title page and chapter effective-date reference; August1,2026 is the separate operations/applicability criterion.
- **Provisions:** Public Law 2025, chapter 768 excludes specified property in data centers beginning operations on or after August 1, 2026, including specified expansion or project property, from the business equipment exemption; excludes services performed at data centers from a Dirigo eligible-sector category and separately excludes data-center businesses beginning operations on or after that date; directs an incentives study and report due November 4, 2026.
- **Mechanism / scope:** incentive_restriction; fiscal
- **Legal effect:** unknown
- **Effective date:** 2026-07-29
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://legislature.maine.gov/legis/bills/display_ps.asp?LD=713&snum=132>)

### LD 912 / SP 402, 132nd Legislature; Public Law 2025, c. 85

- **Policy ID:** `me-ld-912-sp-402-132nd-legislature-public-law-2025-c-85`
- **Sponsor / party:** Sen. Glenn Curry; D (ME Senate Democrat)
- **Recorded status:** Emergency enacted and signed by Governor 2025-05-23, Public Law 2025 c. 85
- **Provisions:** Public Law 2025, chapter 85 adds an exception to the transmission and distribution utility definition for a qualifying commercial or industrial site in the ISO-New England control area, in a municipality north of Chester, historically served without a public utility transmission and distribution plant before December 31, 2018. That exception does not apply if more than 25% of the entity’s nameplate capacity serves data centers on that site.
- **Mechanism / scope:** utility_large_load_restriction; utility_grid

- **Effective date:** 2025-05-23
